scope.description: Whether ordinary replication from a healthy leader repairs a restarted follower's reconstructed configuration, and whether a later configuration entry does. Eleven in-process cases: the nine previously exercised restart shapes plus a follower_in_live_cluster case run with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and disabled. In that case a three-peer cluster removes one peer while keeping three entries of history, the remaining follower is stopped and restarted while the leader keeps leading and replicating, the follower is observed after 400 ms, and the leader then re-adds the removed peer as a new configuration entry and the follower is observed again.
assumptions: Real raft instances in one process over the in-memory transport and the in-memory commit-tracking log store from the captured package; the restarted follower is reconnected to the live leader in both directions.

The restarted follower has no snapshot of its own (snapshot_count 0) and its log already matches the leader's for every entry the leader holds, so no snapshot is shipped and no configuration entry is newly appended before the observation.
The leader stays live and healthy throughout, is in Leader state when the follower is observed, and the new configuration entry is appended by that same leader afterwards.
The observation and repair windows are 400 ms each; the follower's last log index and last applied index are emitted as operands.
excluded: Disk-backed stores, real networks, restarts of more than one member, membership changes between the two observation points other than the single re-add, and any claim about the follower's behaviour while no leader is reachable.

basis.prefix: The new case builds a three-peer cluster with MakeClusterCustom(MakeClusterOpts{Peers: 3, Bootstrap: true, CommitTrackingLogs: true, Conf: inmemConfig with TrailingLogs 10 and RestoreCommittedLogs set per case}), applies 100 commands, calls leader.RemoveServer on one peer, applies ten more entries, and reads the remaining follower's own log configuration entry and tracked commit index plus its snapshot list before stopping only that follower. It emits a follower_inputs CA_EVENT, rebuilds the follower over its own stores on the same address with a fresh in-memory transport reconnected to the live leader in both directions, waits 400 ms, and emits a follower_observation CA_EVENT with the follower's reconstructed configuration index, voter count and server set, its last log and applied indexes, its own log's configuration entry, the leader's state and the leader's configuration. It then calls leader.AddVoter for the removed peer, reads the leader's new configuration index, waits 400 ms and emits a follower_repair CA_EVENT with the new entry index, the follower's reconstructed configuration and the derived repaired flag whose operands are the two indexes and the voter count.
basis.responsibility: NewRaft owns the reconstruction of a node's own configuration from its durable stores, and on a follower that configuration is only rewritten by processing a newly appended configuration entry (or an installed snapshot); the leader's ordinary AppendEntries replication is not responsible for re-deriving it.

comparisons.description: Live-cluster case with the flag enabled: after 400 ms of replication from a leading leader, the follower's reconstructed voter count is compared with the voter count of the configuration entry in its own log.
Control: with the flag disabled the same restarted follower holds the configuration entry's own voter count under the same live leader.
Live-cluster case with the flag enabled: the configuration entry appended afterwards is expected to rewrite the follower's configuration to the new entry index and voter count.
Control: the same appended configuration entry leaves the flag-disabled follower on the new entry index and voter count as well.

before.description: Whether an acknowledged commit taken on a reconstructed smaller configuration is durable on a majority of the committed configuration. Nine in-process cases: the seven previously exercised restart shapes plus a lost_acknowledged_commit case run with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and disabled. In that case a three-voter cluster is left with a single voter, snapshotted, then made three voters again; after every instance is stopped the former leader is restarted, the instance acknowledges one uniquely named commit, the holder is stopped, the other two voters are restarted with the flag disabled, and every store is scanned for that payload before and after the holder rejoins.
assumptions: Real raft instances in one process over the in-memory transport and the in-memory commit-tracking log store from the captured package; the same durable stores are reused across restarts.
The committed configuration of the lost_acknowledged_commit case has three voters while the node's own snapshot metadata carries the demoted configuration with one voter.

The two voters brought back after the acknowledged commit are restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs disabled on purpose, so their own configuration comes from their logs and the second leadership is formed by a majority that never held the payload.
The acknowledged commit is attempted with a 1500 ms timeout, leadership waits use the 3000 ms window, and the payload is searched for across first-index to last-index of each store.
excluded: Disk-backed stores, real networks, crashes during the restart, membership changes after the acknowledged commit, and any comparison of payload contents beyond the exact unique byte string.

prefix.before: The new case runs after the earlier cases in the same test. It builds a three-peer cluster with MakeClusterCustom(MakeClusterOpts{Peers: 3, Bootstrap: true, CommitTrackingLogs: true, Conf: inmemConfig with TrailingLogs 10 and RestoreCommittedLogs set per case}), calls leader.DemoteVoter on both non-leader peers, applies 100 commands, takes leader.Snapshot(), then calls leader.AddVoter for both peers with their addresses and applies five more entries. It emits a lost_inputs CA_EVENT with the last configuration entry (index, decoded server list, voter count), the snapshot metadata's ConfigurationIndex and voter count, and the tracked commit index; it then stops every instance and rebuilds the former leader over its own stores with a fresh in-memory transport. After a bounded leadership wait it applies one uniquely named payload, records whether the future completed and the index it returned, and stops that instance. It rebuilds the other two peers with RestoreCommittedLogs disabled over their own stores, connects the rebuilt instances in both directions, waits for one of them to become leader, and scans both stores for the payload; it then rebuilds the original holder the same way, waits, and scans again. It emits an entry_survival CA_EVENT carrying the reconstructed voter count, the acknowledgement outcome, the payload index, whether the payload remains on the holder after the rejoin, how many of the other voters hold it, the derived durable_on_majority with the copy count, and both terms.

responsibility.before: NewRaft owns the reconstruction of a node's own configuration from its durable stores, and the reconstructed configurations.latest is the only input to the node's own election gating, quorumSize and leader commitment; the committed configuration recorded in the node's own log is the basis on which a client acknowledgement is supposed to be durable.
responsibility.after: NewRaft owns the reconstruction of a node's own configuration from its durable stores, and on a follower that configuration is only rewritten by processing a newly appended configuration entry (or an installed snapshot); the leader's ordinary AppendEntries replication is not responsible for re-deriving it.

before.description: Three-voter case with the flag enabled: the reconstructed voter count is compared with the number of voters in the configuration entry persisted in the node's own log.
Control for the three-voter case: with the flag disabled the reconstructed voter count matches the committed configuration entry.
Three-voter case with the flag enabled: an acknowledged commit is expected to be durable on a majority of the committed configuration rather than on a single copy.
Control for the three-voter case: with the flag disabled the single running member of a three-voter committed configuration cannot acknowledge a commit at all.

after.description: Live-cluster case with the flag enabled: after 400 ms of replication from a leading leader, the follower's reconstructed voter count is compared with the voter count of the configuration entry in its own log.
Control: with the flag disabled the same restarted follower holds the configuration entry's own voter count under the same live leader.
Live-cluster case with the flag enabled: the configuration entry appended afterwards is expected to rewrite the follower's configuration to the new entry index and voter count.
Control: the same appended configuration entry leaves the flag-disabled follower on the new entry index and voter count as well.

revision_reason: Adds the follower_in_live_cluster case with its flag-disabled control: with a live leading leader and a leader-side RemoveServer committed beforehand, only the remaining follower is restarted, observed after ordinary replication, and then observed again after the leader appends a new configuration entry. Replaces the comparison set with this case's reconstruction and repair predicates.
